mark_split.label: Reduce to a quadratic in sinθ
Check and write the general solution

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.106, chapter 9 TRIGONOMETRIC EQUATIONS, Short Answer question 1(iii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 shape rewards the four separable moves — clear the denominators while recording the condition they impose, reduce to a quadratic in sinθ, discard the out-of-range root in writing, and finish with the correct sine general solution. EXTRANEOUS-ROOT RECORD: multiplying by sinθ cosθ can admit values where sinθ cosθ = 0, so those were tested. Neither sinθ = 0 nor cosθ = 0 satisfies the cleared equation sin²θ + 3cos²θ = 5 sinθ (they give 3 = 0 and 1 = ±5), and the surviving root sinθ = 1/2 forces cosθ = ±√3/2, so the whole family θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/6) lies inside the domain. Both θ = π/6 and θ = 5π/6 were substituted into the ORIGINAL equation and both give ±10/√3 on each side, so NOTHING is discarded here except sinθ = −3, which is out of the sine range. The card therefore states the check and its result rather than inventing a rejection. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Equations supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Clear the fractions
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write all three ratios in sine and cosine, then multiply by sinθ cosθ. Record θ ≠ nπ/2 now — that condition is what you test the answer against at the end.
steps.memory_tip: Write everything over sinθ and cosθ, then multiply by sinθ cosθ. Record sinθ ≠ 0 and cosθ ≠ 0 first.

recall.must_convey: That all three ratios are written in sine and cosine and both sides are multiplied by sinθ cosθ, with sinθ ≠ 0 and cosθ ≠ 0 recorded.

steps.why: The three ratios are fractions in sinθ and cosθ. Multiplying by sinθ cosθ removes every denominator, but it is only allowed while sinθ ≠ 0 and cosθ ≠ 0, so that condition is written down before it is used.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by cosθ only and leaving the cotθ term as a fraction.
Not recording that sinθ and cosθ must not be zero.

steps.label: Reduce to a quadratic in sinθ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Replace cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ and collect. Bring every term to one side so the quadratic has a positive sin²θ coefficient.
steps.memory_tip: Replace cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ, then move everything to the side that keeps sin²θ positive.

recall.must_convey: That cos²θ is replaced by 1 − sin²θ, giving 2sin²θ + 5 sinθ − 3 = 0.

steps.why: One ratio is needed before anything can be factorised. Replacing cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ leaves an ordinary quadratic that behaves like any other.
common_mistakes: Sign slip when moving 5 sinθ across.
Replacing sin²θ instead and leaving a cosine behind.

steps.label: Reject the impossible root
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and the part most often skipped. sinθ = −3 lies outside [−1, 1], so that branch is discarded with the reason written down.
steps.memory_tip: Split the middle term as 6 − 1. Then sinθ = −3 is outside [−1, 1], so discard it IN WRITING.

recall.must_convey: That the quadratic factorises to (2sinθ − 1)(sinθ + 3) = 0 and sinθ = −3 is rejected because |sinθ| ≤ 1.

steps.why: A quadratic gives two roots, but a sine only takes values from −1 to 1. Testing each root against that range, in writing, is part of solving a trigonometric equation.
common_mistakes: Carrying sinθ = −3 forward and inventing an angle for it.
Discarding it with no reason written down.

steps.label: Check and write the general solution
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Clearing the fractions could have let in values where sinθ or cosθ is zero, so test the surviving root against θ ≠ nπ/2 before writing the answer. It passes, so the whole family is kept.
steps.memory_tip: Before writing the answer, put the root back: sinθ = 1/2 gives cosθ = ±√3/2, so no denominator is zero.
lines: Neither is zero, so θ ≠ nπ/2 holds and this

steps.why: Multiplying by sinθ cosθ can let in values where sinθ or cosθ is zero, and at those values tanθ, cotθ and secθ do not exist. Testing the surviving root against that condition is what makes the answer safe to write.
common_mistakes: Using the cosine form 2nπ ± α for a sine equation.
Never checking that cosθ is not zero after clearing the fractions.
